text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 11 in history:
1488 - James III of Scotland was murdered after his defeat at the Battle of Sauchieburn, Stirling, and was succeeded by his son, James IV.
1509 - King Henry VIII of England married the first of his six wives, Catherine of Aragon.
1572 - Ben Jonson, English poet and playwright, notably for "Every Man In His Humour" and "Volpone", born.
1727 - King George I, first Hanoverian king of Great Britain (1714-27), died and was succeeded by his son George II.
1776 - John Constable, English landscape painter, born. His most important works include "The Hay-Wain" and "Dedham Vale: Morning".
1847 - Sir John Franklin, English naval officer and Arctic explorer, died in Canada attempting to discover the Northwest Passage.
1864 - Richard Strauss, German composer of operas including "Salome", "Der Rosenkavalier" and "Elektra", born.

1880 - Jeanette Rankin, first woman member of the U.S. Congress, born. A lifetime pacifist, she was the only legislator to vote against the declaration of war against Japan after the raid on Pearl Harbour.
1895 - Nikolai Bulganin, Soviet prime minister from 1955-58, born.
1903 - King Alexander I and Queen Draga of Serbia were murdered in a coup.
1910 - Jacques-Yves Cousteau, French underwater explorer and inventor of the aqualung diving apparatus, born.
1955 - Eighty people were killed and over 100 injured when three cars crashed on the Le Mans racetrack in France and ploughed into the spectators' grandstand.
1963 - Governor George Wallace allowed the enrolment of two black students at the University of Alabama after he had first blocked their entry by standing in front of the door.
1963 - Greek Prime Minister Constantine Karamanlis resigned.
1970 - Alexander Feodorovich Kerensky, Russian politician and prime minister, died. Deposed by the Bolsheviks in 1917, he fled to France and then to the United States.
1977 - Dutch marines stormed a train at Assen in which South Mouluccan terrorists had been holding more than 50 hostages for 19 days. Six terrorists and two hostages were killed.
1979 - John Wayne (Marion Michael Morrison), U.S. film star, died. Despite being the biggest box office draw in cinema history, he won only one Oscar for best actor ("True Grit".
1981 - In Iran, over 1,000 people were killed in an earthquake measuring 6.8 on the Richter scale. The town of Golbaf in Kerman province was destroyed.

1984 - Enrico Berlinguer, leader of the Italian Communist Party, died. For 12 years he led the largest Communist party in Western Europe and led it away from Soviet influence but failed to bring it to power in Italy.
1993 - Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani won a second four-year term as president of Iran.
1994 - Seoul, Washington and Tokyo agreed to push for measured sanctions against North Korea for its refusal to allow international inspection of its nuclear programme.
